Source Code


Introduction
This showcase presents my analysis of the UK 2024 General Election, examining voter turnout patterns across constituencies and countries. Using official election data, I explored how turnout varies geographically and what this reveals about political engagement across the United Kingdom.
The Code
Here’s the code I used to clean and analyze UK election data:
​```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
Load UK election data
uk_csv <- “candidate-level-results-general-election-04-07-2024.csv”
uk_raw <- readr::read_csv(uk_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
Clean column names
names(uk_raw) <- names(uk_raw) %>%
tolower() %>%
str_replace_all(“\s+”, “_“)
Filter and aggregate by constituency
uk1 <- uk_raw %>% filter(!election_is_by-election)
uk2 <- uk1 %>%
select(
constituency = constituency_name,
country_name,
valid_votes = candidate_vote_count,
electorate
)
uk3 <- uk2 %>%
group_by(country_name, constituency) %>%
summarise(
valid_votes = sum(valid_votes, na.rm = TRUE),
electorate = max(electorate, na.rm = TRUE),
.groups = “drop”
)
Calculate turnout
uk <- uk3 %>%
mutate(turnout_registered = 100 * valid_votes / electorate) %>%
filter(is.finite(turnout_registered), electorate > 0)
Compute country-level statistics
turnout_by_country <- uk %>%
group_by(country_name) %>%
summarise(
mean_turnout = mean(turnout_registered, na.rm = TRUE),
median_turnout = median(turnout_registered, na.rm = TRUE),
n = n(),
.groups = “drop”
) %>%
arrange(desc(mean_turnout))
turnout_by_country
​```
The Visualization
This visualization compares mean and median voter turnout across the four UK countries:
​{r, fig.cap="UK 2024 Election turnout by country", fig.width=8, fig.height=5} ggplot(turnout_by_country, aes(x = reorder(country_name, mean_turnout), y = mean_turnout)) +   geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = "#0072B2") +   geom_point(aes(y = median_turnout), color = "red", size = 3) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100),                      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +   labs(     title = "UK 2024 General Election: Mean & Median Turnout by Country",     subtitle = "Bars = mean turnout; Red points = median turnout",     x = "Country",     y = "Turnout (% of registered voters)"   ) +   theme_minimal() ​
Explanation: This figure reveals important patterns in UK political engagement. England shows the highest mean turnout at approximately 60%, followed closely by Scotland at 59%. Wales and Northern Ireland show slightly lower turnout rates around 56-57%. The red points indicate median turnout, which helps us understand the distribution - when median and mean are similar, turnout is relatively consistent across constituencies within that country.
The analysis demonstrates that smaller areas outside major cities tend to have higher turnout rates, whilst large urban constituencies typically show lower engagement. This pattern likely reflects differences in community cohesion, with smaller, more tightly-knit areas fostering greater civic participation. The visualization uses bars ordered by mean turnout for easy comparison, and the dual representation of mean and median provides a more complete picture than either measure alone would offer.
Key Findings
The main takeaways from this analysis were:
England achieved the highest average turnout, though differences between countries were relatively modest
Urban constituencies consistently showed lower turnout than smaller, rural areas
The similarity between mean and median values suggests turnout patterns are fairly consistent within each country
Source Code
The complete code and analysis are available in my GitHub repository.
